description:

The split was forced by a measured path-cap breach, not a preference: registration alone touches ten-plus files before the handler itself, and the global rail says that is a split signal at plan time rather than a discovery for a worker at step 5.

ORDERING IS A SAFETY CONSTRAINT, NOT PAPERWORK. This row lands SECOND. An unregistered handler module is inert; a registered kind with no handler is a decode path that accepts a command nothing serves. Do not start this row until task-b2548479 has committed `apps/daemon/src/cutover/cutover-activate-service.ts` and its bridge.

- `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.ts:135` — composes the handler tables (`...BOOTSTRAP_HANDLERS, ...GOAL_HANDLERS, ...PLANNING_HANDLERS`); add the cutover table here.
- `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.test.ts:310` and `:318` — `ROWS` and `REGISTRATION_ORDER` each `toHaveLength(38)` -> 39, and :488-489 pin `OPERATOR_ONLY` at 7.

WHAT IS ALREADY DONE AND MUST NOT BE REDONE: `cutover.activate` is ALREADY in `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS` and ALREADY published in the generated client (`packages/control-room-client/src/generated/generated-client.ts:188` and `:290`). Epic rail 7B is bounded to the daemon-side rosters listed above — but re-measure that claim before relying on it, and if a generated artifact DOES derive from the daemon roster, declare it as an owned path in the same commit rather than leaving it stale.

definitionOfDone: VERIFY-OR-BLOCK at claim, recorded in a row comment (not the completion summary, which is write-only and persists nowhere): the handler module `apps/daemon/src/cutover/cutover-activate-service.ts` EXISTS AND IS COMMITTED — prove with `git cat-file -e HEAD:apps/daemon/src/cutover/cutover-activate-service.ts` or `git ls-files --error-unmatch`, never with `git log -- <path>`. If it is present on disk but untracked, that is a DIFFERENT block: report it as an uncommitted-deliverable block naming task-b2548479, and do not commit another row's paths. Also confirm `git grep -n '"cutover.activate"' -- apps/daemon/src` still shows no registry entry, else adopt rather than duplicate.

`"cutover.activate"` is added to BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_KINDS, a PAYLOAD_KEYS entry is declared for it in daemon-command-vocabulary.ts, and the handler table is composed into daemon-command-registry.ts:135 — with EVERY named count consumer updated in the SAME commit: bootstrap-services.test.ts:79 OWNED_KINDS set-equality, daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts:186, daemon-command-registry.test.ts:310 and :318. A commit that lands the roster without its consumers leaves the suite red for everyone on the branch.

The roster guard is BIDIRECTIONAL, not a subset check: assert that every advertised kind is served by the dispatch seam AND every served kind is advertised, enumerating the served set from the registry's own handler composition rather than from the roster constant. A test that iterates the roster alone cannot see a served-but-unadvertised kind, and deleting an entry shrinks its own iteration while staying green.

An end-to-end arm drives `cutover.activate` through the production registry path (not the handler in isolation) and asserts it REACHES the handler — proven by the handler's own refusal code and layer surfacing from the registry, not by the absence of a decode error. A decode-only arm cannot distinguish 'registered and served' from 'registered and silently unhandled'.

PAYLOAD_KEYS is an exact ordered allow-list: assert a hostile extra key is refused with its exact stable code and refusing layer, and that the declared key roster matches the handler's admitted surface in both directions.

STEP 4 — THE BIDIRECTIONAL ROSTER GUARD AND THE PAYLOAD FENCE.

(A) BIDIRECTIONAL, NOT A SUBSET CHECK — this is the arm that makes the registration durable. Assert that every ADVERTISED kind is SERVED by the dispatch seam AND every SERVED kind is ADVERTISED, as a set-equality. Enumerate the SERVED set from the registry's own handler composition (the thing that actually dispatches), NOT from the roster constant. A test that iterates the roster alone can only see one direction: deleting an entry shrinks its own iteration and stays green while a served capability silently vanishes from the advertised surface — and the mirror case, a served-but-unadvertised kind, is invisible to it entirely.
bootstrap-services.test.ts:79 already does a set-equality against a HAND-MAINTAINED list; that is not the same guarantee, because both sides are hand-written. The new arm must derive one side from the implementation seam.

(B) THE PAYLOAD FENCE: assert a hostile extra key on a `cutover.activate` payload is refused with its exact stable code AND refusing layer, and that the declared PAYLOAD_KEYS roster matches the handler's admitted surface in BOTH directions — no declared key the handler ignores, no admitted key the roster omits. A one-directional check lets the roster drift from the handler silently.

(C) OPERATOR-ONLY, if step 3(E) placed the kind there: assert it is refused for a non-operator principal with the exact code and layer, and that the OPERATOR_ONLY count and the filtered-ROWS count at registry.test.ts:488/:489 agree. RESTORE PROTOCOL: every file this row touches is TRACKED, so `git diff --exit-code -- <path>` IS a valid restore proof — but only if the path was clean when you started. Check `git status --porcelain` per path FIRST; for any path already dirty, back it up to `%TEMP%/b8272ee0-<workerId>/` and prove the restore by SHA256 equality in a call SEPARATE from the restore (64 hex, non-empty, equal). If it reds on decode, the arm is testing the roster rather than the dispatch and is not the guard it claims to be.
D2 THE BIDIRECTIONAL GUARD SEES BOTH WAYS — two separate drills, one degree of freedom each. Remove the kind from the ADVERTISED roster while leaving it served -> step 4(A) reds. Restore. Remove it from the SERVED composition while leaving it advertised -> step 4(A) reds again. A guard that only catches one direction is a subset check wearing a set-equality's clothes.
D3 THE PAYLOAD FENCE: add a key to PAYLOAD_KEYS that the handler does not admit -> step 4(B)'s both-directions arm reds.

A GREEN drill is a FINDING to report in the row comment, never a pass to bank.

planningNotes.risks: (1) REGISTERING BEFORE THE HANDLER EXISTS IS FAIL-OPEN and is the risk this whole plan is ordered around: the kind becomes decodable and routes through the registry with nothing to serve it, on the one-way GA activation surface. Step 1(a) blocks on `git cat-file -e HEAD:<handler>` and must be honoured even though the governor's unpark is impatient — the orphaned reducer is real, but the fix is to land the handler, not to register ahead of it. (2) THE HAND-MAINTAINED MIRROR at bootstrap-services.test.ts:46 is the single most likely omission: :79's set-equality passes only because BOTH sides moved, so a worker who edits the roster and re-runs sees green from :79 while :81's count fails, and may 'fix' the count without adding the mirror entry. D4 drills exactly this. (3) A SUBSET CHECK WEARING A SET-EQUALITY'S CLOTHES: :79 compares two HAND-WRITTEN lists, which proves they agree, not that the advertised set equals the SERVED set. Step 4(A) must derive one side from the registry's dispatch composition, and D2 drills BOTH directions separately. (4) A DECODE-ONLY END-TO-END ARM cannot distinguish 'registered and served' from 'registered and silently unhandled' — the arm must assert the HANDLER'S OWN refusal code and layer, and D1 proves it reds for the right reason. (5) THE bootstrap-contracts.ts COLLISION with task-0ca390d9 is live at plan time; editing a contested frozen tuple concurrently produces swept work. Stop and report rather than racing. (6) PARTIAL LANDING: a commit that adds the roster entry without moving all seven counts leaves the daemon suite red for everyone on the branch. All of it or none of it. (7) OPERATOR_ONLY is a DECISION, not a default — a one-way GA activation reachable by a non-operator principal is a finding. (8) DO NOT REGENERATE the client, MCP schemas or digest mirrors; re-measure first, and if one DOES derive from the daemon roster, own it and regenerate in the same commit — a stale generated artifact is worse than an unregistered kind. (9) A GATE ON A STALE SHA false-blocked the sibling row today; re-capture HEAD at gate time and pair absence claims with positive controls.
